title: Lire + Elvira
author: glvno
notes: 8 Lire and Elvira 2 layered on one keyboard: every key plays a Lire voice and an Elvira voice at once. Both are cut down to fit the FM-1: Lire keeps four of its eight voices (one pair from each quad, still cross-modulating, with SHARP, MOD and HOLD per pair, the Hyper LFO and the delay); Elvira keeps its four voices but loses its SRR stage and its own delay. A two-row Mix (LIRE, ELVIRA) sets the balance. Keys F3..G5 sound.

title: Sol 29N
author: michael glaviano
notes: Recalls the Elta Music Solar 42N, a stereo drone and ambient machine. Three drones of up to five detuned saws each swell in through their own AR envelopes while FX, LFO or EDIT is held (set a button to switch and it is the drone's HOLD); ARP plays the two noise voices the same way (bursts: noise stepped by a sample & hold; bleeps: a tone whose pitch a second sample & hold of the noise steps). AUTO, the Mod device's first page, brings back the slow pulse generators that swell the drones on their own (on when the patch opens). The keys play one voice of a morphing wavetable with a square sub and pulse-width modulation, and PLAY runs a 5-step line through it. Each side has a 12 dB band-pass filter, swept together by an LFO and a looping envelope that follows drone A, then a distortion with a dry / distorted balance (DIST L / R, GAIN L / R), as on the original; a long reverb feeds a ping-pong delay.

title: Sol 29N XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: The browser's full version of Sol 29N, after the Elta Music SOLAR 42N's manual and panel (eltamusic.com). Six drones: 1, 2, 4 and 5 are five saws each, two low, one mid, two high, each with its own tuning, micro-tuning and level (0 = muted), tuned to chords across the registers; VOLT transposes all five down and past half its travel makes them frequency-modulate each other; MOD puts LFO A into their pitch. Drones 3 and 6 are the 'Papa Srapa' noise voices: a square modulator frequency- and / or amplitude-modulates a tone oscillator, plus white noise and a sample & hold of the noise, clocked by the modulator, into the tone's pitch. Each drone has its own AR envelope: play them on the keys C2 D2 E2 F2 G2 A2 (the drone keypad), on FX / LFO / EDIT (drones 1, 2, 4) and ARP (3 and 6), latch them with HOLD, or let AUTO (Mod) swell them on their own pulse generators. The keys from C3 up play VCO A + B as one voice: two morphing wavetable oscillators, A cross-modulating B, a sub (pulse width moved by LFO A) that A can be synced to, each with its own ADSR with HOLD and a self-cycling option, and glide; PLAY runs the 5-step LINE through them. LFO A and B (positive only). A mixer with VOL and PAN per channel into a dual 12 dB filter (LP or BP per side, MOD L from LFO A, MOD R from LFO B, LINK hands R the left side's modulation), a distortion after it (DIST = dry / distorted balance, GAIN), and a shimmer on each side, slightly different (a reverb with an octave-up granular pitch shift in its feedback; rows decay, octave mix, tone, wet). Substitutes and omissions: the light sensor and CV MOD are LFO A; the self-cycling envelopes loop on a pulse generator, not on their own end; the contact mic, its envelope follower, the external input, the joystick, the drone DIVIDER, the touch keyboard's arpeggiator, quantiser, vibrato and pressure output and the cartridge choice are left out. Browser only (SANDBOX).

title: Lire + Elvira XL
author: glvno
notes: The full versions of Lire + Elvira: 8 Lire XL and Elvira 2 XL layered on one keyboard, for the browser only (a sandbox patch, far over the FM-1's limits). Every white key plays a Lire voice and an Elvira voice at once: all eight Lire voices, with SHARP, MOD and the FM or LFO source per pair, HOLD and PITCH per group, the FM structure switch, TOTAL FB, VIBRATO, the Hyper LFO and the two delay lines before the distortion; all four Elvira voices with their MOD programs (SRR, bits, noise), the saturated mix, the ladder low pass, the delay up to 1.6 s, OUCH with its feedback loop, both LFOs into any of six destinations and a step sequence per voice that plays with the transport. A two-row Mix (LIRE, ELVIRA) sets the balance. Keys E2..A6 sound.

title: Babushka
author: fairplay
notes: Benjolin-like assembly and patch built upon Matryoshka engine

title: Hera 4
author: michael glaviano
notes: Juno-106 panel, four voices (the original has six; Hera 6 XL plays six in the browser). MIDI CC 64 is the hold pedal; Output sets volume. Poly 2 steals when all voices are busy. HPF 2/3 and chorus II settings are approximated by ear. Patch shift, tape, memory and the MIDI function switch are hardware or storage, not reproduced.

title: Canvas
author: michael glaviano
notes: Music Easel patch field with four independent random outputs. Select PATCH to connect any control source to an input. FX fires the pulser. The Arpeggiator has a rate input in Hz. Missing: external audio/preamp/envelope detector and linear decay. Pulse/wave rows use numbers; sine is extra. Plates, trims, program cards and local/remote switching need hardware or storage. Low range starts at 0.22 Hz, not 0.17. Output split remains unverified.

title: Io 4
author: michael glaviano
notes: Jupiter-4 architecture, four voices. UNISON ON is UNISON I; SHARE is UNISON II: one key uses four voices, two keys use two each, three or four use one each. Assignment still uses separate assign and unison rows. Other control gaps remain under the 1.5 fidelity audit.

title: Drift Poly
author: michael glaviano
notes: The drift poly engine as made, so its presets (PRESET on its page) are at hand on the FM-1.

title: Supersaw Stack
author: michael glaviano
notes: The supersaw stack engine as made, so its presets (PRESET on its page) are at hand on the FM-1.

title: 8 Lire XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: The SOMA Lyra-8 after its manual (v2.1). The card is its 46 controls: TUNE per voice (continuous); source (FM / off / LFO), MOD, SHARP, FAST per pair; HOLD, PITCH per group; 34>56 78>12, TOTAL FB, VIBRATO; the Hyper LFO; the MOD DELAY; the DISTORTION. The rear jacks are inputs; the Lyra switches them by plugging, here a crossfader inside the assembly (0 = unplugged). Not here: outside audio into EXT IN (no audio input module), the plates' skin response (velocity and aftertouch stand in).

title: 808 Kit XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: Every TR-808 voice, knob and switch. Two tracks: DRUMS (the 808 Kit's rows) and DRUMS 2 (mid tom, hi tom, cymbal, ACCENT). Only the AC row accents (by the accent level), as on the TR-808. Switches: tom / conga for the three toms, rim shot / claves, hand clap / maracas. pre-scale sets both tracks' rate. The step count is each track's len: set them alike. Not here: the rhythm memory (A / B variations, fill-ins, auto fill, rhythm tracks).

title: 909 Kit XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: Every TR-909 drum, knob and pattern feature. Three tracks: DRUMS (the 909 Kit's rows), DRUMS 2 (mid tom, crash, ride, ACCENT), FLAM (kick, snare, toms). The crash and ride stand in for samples. Card accent flam: TOTAL ACCENT, FLAM, SHUFFLE and SCALE for all three tracks; kick, snare, toms and closed hat also accent on velocity 127. The hats share one level (hihat card). LAST STEP is each track's len: set them alike.

title: Algo Four XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: DX100 panel; one OP picker selects all fourteen operator controls. LFO SPEED covers 0.0008–55 Hz. AR/D1R/D2R use 0..31 rates: zero stops the stage; D2R zero holds D1L. D1L/RR use 0..15. Rate scaling uses 0..3. PB MODE selects LOW/HIGH/KON. Breath uses CC 2; foot uses CC 64. Ratio has the original 64 choices; detune has -3..+3 positions (up to 2.6 cents). Bend uses octaves. Cartridge, MIDI settings and stored patch memory are hardware/storage, not reproduced.

title: Briefcase 3 XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: EMS VCS3 with all 256 matrix pins, 0 out/1 in. Missing engine abilities: external audio (input 1 carries keys, input 2 is silent), envelope repeat and decay beyond 10 s, variable sine/triangle shapes, and the 18 dB filter (24 dB here). The scope replaces the meter; speaker switches, headphone/control outputs and keyboard sockets are hardware, not reproduced. Output filters are flat at 0.5; pan is 0 left/1 right.

title: Elvira 2 XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: Elmyra 2 controls with eleven MODP programs, twelve filter types, microtonal scales, effects, two LFOs and patch jacks. BITMANGLER uses 16-bit XOR; the original's exact mask sequence is unverified. Missing: outside audio, control-motion recording and the full 128-step TUNE sequencer. The sequence here has eight steps. Browser only.

title: Expander S XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: The Oberheim Eight Voice: eight SEMs, each with every knob of its own (two VCOs with FM / PWM from an envelope or its LFO and sync, the saw / pulse mixer, the 12 dB VCF from low pass through notch to high pass or band pass, two ADS envelopes, VCA on, level and pan), an all-SEMs row per control that moves all eight at once, played by the keyboard: unison, assign, split with its own unison per half, portamento per half, octave, tune, VCF. Not here: the jacks, the R/C assign mode.

title: Hera 6 XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: Juno-106 panel, six voices. MIDI CC 64 is the hold pedal; Output sets volume. Poly 2 steals when all voices are busy; its card still needs to select no-steal with Poly 2. HPF 2/3 and chorus II settings are approximated by ear. Patch shift, tape, memory and the MIDI function switch are hardware or storage, not reproduced.

title: Meridian 8 XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: The Landscape NOON, after its manual. The card is its 58 controls: per channel main, secondary, volume, MOD, mute and CV mute; nine LINK buttons; the main volume. Patch points are ports: gate 1..8 (any voltage powers its channel: drones), odd / even cv, audio (opened by the 1-2 link; patch an output 1..8 into it for internal processing), outputs 1..8, l, r. Aftertouch presses all touch plates. Not here: audio from outside the browser; plug-sensing outputs (a level and a mono Macro stand in).

title: Oracle V XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: The Prophet-5 Rev 4 whole (Sequential Prophet-5 User’s Guide): oscillator A saw and pulse, B saw, triangle and pulse, each on or off, sync, B’s keyboard switch and lo freq; the Rev 1/2 and Rev 3 filters, keyboard amount, velocity and aftertouch, the Release switch; Poly Mod (filter envelope and oscillator B into A’s frequency, pulse width and the filter, at audio rate) and Wheel-Mod (LFO saw / triangle / square, 0.022 to 500 Hz, or noise into both frequencies, both pulse widths and the filter);

title: Perun 4 XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: After the PERKONS HD-01 manual (1.3): per voice 3 algorithms of 3 modes (CHORD, DIGITAL NOISE too), param 1 / 2, tune, decay, drone, cutoff, VCF LP / BP / HP, drive, send, level. The mod LFO (7 waves, sync) reaches all 8 knobs of each voice; control all; quantiser. Each voice has a track (VOICE 1..4: length, rate, play mode, swing, chance, accent, tune lock), rates ÷8..x4, groove, fills (C4..F4). Mod sync x8..÷8. BBD: colour, vintage, sync to 1/1D; compressor. Switches step, never blend. Not her

title: Spokes 6 XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: After the Elektron Model:Cycles manual: six tracks, each able to play any of the six FM machines (kick, snare, metal, perc, tone, chord: pitch, decay, color, shape, sweep, contour), with fine tune, level, volume + dist, pan, delay and reverb sends, punch, gate mode, chance, mute, retrigs (rate to a 1/128 triplet, length or INF, fade) and an LFO (speed or a tempo multiple, backward, start phase, wave, depth, trig mode, envelope wave, fade in / out) and velocity, each reaching appendix B's destina

title: Verona Drum 1 XL
author: michael glaviano
notes: The whole Vermona DRM1 MKIV: all eight channels with every knob, PAN and VOLUME each, MASTER. The rows are the TRIG buttons; a hi-hat row plays open or closed by its TRIG switch, and the CLOSED track plays both hi-hats closed (the original's second MIDI note per hi-hat).
